_comment: THE SIX. The front of the platform: the front page and /sectors render these and
nothing else. Specified in eufabric-page-specifications.md §4.2, which is the
authority for this file — instances, sector edges, the boundary rule and the
rendering rule are all settled there.
WHY A NODE KIND AND NOT SIX SECTOR KEYS. The sector spine in data/sectors.json is
keyed on FIGARO industries because the input-output joins depend on that keying.
Hydrogen and circular materials are not FIGARO industries; a pseudo-key for either
would corrupt the join. So the ecosystem sits above the spine and points into it,
and an instance with no sector edge at all is a first-class instance rather than an
incomplete one.
THE FIELDS
id          the instance, and the tile's key. Never a sector slug: `chemicals`
spans two slugs and `batteries` covers part of one.
name        what the tile says.
icon        which drawing from the set in web/components/SectorIcon.tsx. Named
rather than derived from the id, because the icons are keyed by the
noun they draw and four of the six borrow a sector's.
sectors     the sector edges, [] where the instance has none.
sector_scope  a sentence, where the sector edge is WIDER than the instance.
Only `batteries` carries one today: FIGARO's batsol covers batteries
and solar, the instance covers batteries, and solar stays in the
register with no ecosystem edge. Null where the edge is exact — a
scope note on an exact edge would read as a caveat on a fact that
does not need one.
technology, project, measure, material
explicit edges, for the instances that have no sector key and are
DEFINED by them. Empty today for both: hydrogen and circular
materials have no dataset yet, and an edge list invented ahead of
the data would be the tile promising a page that does not exist.
WHAT IS NOT HERE. Carbon capture. It was on the first list of six and it is the one
entry that is not an industry: it is an abatement route several industries take, so
it is a technology node with edges from cement, steel and chemicals, and the CO2
transport and storage projects that serve them are shared project nodes.
THE BOUNDARY RULE, GATED IN sources/check_sector_schema.py. A project belongs to
the ecosystem whose product it makes. A recycling plant is circular-materials; a
recycled-content obligation on a producing sector stays in that sector with an edge
to circular-materials. Two ecosystem edges on one project fail the build unless the
project is flagged `shared` — which is what a CO2 store serving three industries is,
and what a plant making one product is not.
ORDER IS RENDER ORDER. Cement first because it is the one that is built; the rest
in the order brief 4 §2 lists them.

ecosystems.name: Chemicals
ecosystems.sector_scope: Organic chemicals and plastics. Fertilisers are excluded; ammonia and the fertiliser line are read under hydrogen.

ecosystems.name: Batteries
ecosystems.sector_scope: Batteries only. The sector key covers batteries and solar because FIGARO does; solar stays in the register and carries no ecosystem edge.
